title: Everton hopeful of keeping Jack Grealish beyond end of loan spell
content:
Everton are hopeful of keeping Jack Grealish at the club beyond the end of this season.

The 30-year-old is on loan at the Merseyside club from Manchester City, with the deal including an option to buy in the region of £50million ($67.3m).

Everton are keen on keeping Grealish, who has not played since January 18 due to a foot injury that required surgery, but are likely to regard the purchase option as being too expensive, according to sources with knowledge of the club’s situation.

Another loan move could be a more likely route to retaining Grealish, though talks over a deal are not expected to progress until the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

Grealish made 20 Premier League appearances for Everton before undergoing surgery, scoring twice and recording six assists from the left wing.

Manager David Moyes said in January that he did not expect Grealish to play again this season.

“It’s really disappointing for the player, as for the club and all of us here because he’s such an important part,” Moyes said at the time. “He’s a big character, big experience for us and we’ll miss him. He’s done a lot of good things for us.”

Grealish signed for City in August 2021 for a then-British record of £100m. He has made 157 appearances for the club and was part of their treble-winning campaign in 2021-22, but fell out of favour under Pep Guardiola last season, only making seven starts in the Premier League.

He has made 39 appearances for England, scoring four times, but has not appeared for the side since October 2024 and has not been called up by current head coach Thomas Tuchel.

Everton are next in action away at Brentford on Saturday April 11.

Analysis by Everton correspondent Patrick Boyland

It should come as little surprise that Everton are plotting to bring Grealish back to the club next season. He made an instant impression on Merseyside, setting up Iliman Ndiaye’s goal against Brighton & Hove Albion on his first start, and registered six assists in 20 games prior to sustaining the foot injury that is expected to keep him out for the rest of the campaign.

It is telling that the 30-year-old has stayed at Everton instead of returning to parent club City for his rehabilitation. That in itself is unusual and a sign both of Everton’s commitment to the player and Grealish’s happiness on Merseyside. He has enjoyed his time at the club, plunging himself into community schemes, and has often been seen signing autographs for fans late at night after games.

The £50m option fee in the loan agreement is unrealistic given his age and sizeable wage packet of around £300,000. He will also head into the final year of his City deal this summer.

It is still early days, but there is hope an arrangement can be found to prolong his stay. And that would likely be a popular move indeed where most Everton fans are concerned.
